what_it_measures: how many games a player was available for
supporting_statistic: every candidate cross-position transformation correlates with games played at rho 0.14 to 0.30
justification: Games played is the one quantity in this project that is unambiguously comparable across every role: a game is a game. It is READY as a DENOMINATOR and as a disclosure.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: It is not READY as a value input. Every season-total measure already rewards availability implicitly, and a model that also adds it is counting durability twice. Whether an award SHOULD reward availability is a question about the award, not about the data.

what_it_measures: goals, one-point goals, two-point goals and PLL points a player actually recorded
supporting_statistic: PLL points reconcile exactly to the official final score in every eligible team-game in all five seasons (Phase 9 check 7; the single documented exception is archers-cannons-2022-6-18)
justification: It is OBSERVED, fully attributed, and needs no model. It is the only input in this table that requires no estimation of any kind.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: It is production, not ability, and it is not comparable across roles: a goalie's scoring production is zero by job description, not by performance.

what_it_measures: empirical-Bayes shrunk career rates for shooting, one-point conversion, faceoff, save and turnover tendency
supporting_statistic: 239 of 419 players reach reliability 0.5 on at least one rate; leave-one-season-out rank correlation never falls below 0.84
justification: Career pooling is the only aggregation that improves identification: pooling player-SEASONS as rows makes it worse (shooting kappa 70.8 -> 145.5, zero of 863 clearing the gate), pooling a player's CAREER makes it better. The estimates recompute exactly from the published successes and trials.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: A career estimate answers 'how good has this player been across 2022-2026', not 'how good is he now'. Ageing, role change and team context are modelled nowhere. 44 players changed listed position and 97 changed team inside the window.

what_it_measures: points per offensive possession, and every other possession-denominated team rate
supporting_statistic: 2023 moves from 96.96 to 91.39 possessions per game and from 0.2520 to 0.2674 points per possession under the evidence-bounded repair; 2022, 2025 and 2026 are bit-identical
justification: Phase 9 classified 2023 per-possession metrics NON_COMPARABLE. Phase 10 found the cause -- 201 post-goal faceoffs ordered before their own goal in 12 games -- and repaired it from the feed's own markerId sequence. After repair 2023 sits inside the five-season range on every possession metric and team rankings do not move at all.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: The repaired layer is published as possessions_repaired.csv and the frozen possessions.csv is unchanged, so any cross-season possession-denominated comparison must state WHICH layer it used. 89 2023 goals still have no faceoff logged after them, against 39 in 2026 and 51 in 2022, so a residual excess remains.

what_it_measures: points produced on a player's own shot attempts against what league-average shots of the same class produce
supporting_statistic: single-season kappa 70.8 shots with 13 of 192 players clearing reliability 0.5; league components sum to zero to 10 decimal places
justification: The VALUE accounting is exact and unbiased -- it is arithmetic on observed shots against a measured league baseline. What is unreliable is reading it as ability at one season's sample.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: A single season's shooting value is dominated by conversion luck. Phase 7 measured the consequence: replacing the shooting component with its shrunk equivalent moves 219 of 228 total-value ranks.

what_it_measures: turnovers committed against the position group's turnovers-per-touch rate, priced at the empirical forward-window cost of a turnover
supporting_statistic: career kappa 138.0 touches; 218 of 419 players (52.0%) clear reliability 0.5 -- the highest count of any rate
justification: Turnover tendency is the best-evidenced player rate in the framework after faceoff win percentage, and it is already residualised against a position-group baseline, so the role effect is out of the expectation.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: Roughly 19% of the league's turnovers name only a team, so every player's absolute turnover count is understated. The ratio is internally consistent because both sides of it are built from player-attributed sums, but the level is not the official level.

what_it_measures: two-point goals, two-point attempts, the PLL points they generated and how often a player chose the long shot
supporting_statistic: 2465 career attempts across 271 shooters; the league two-point return is +0.0004 points per attempt against the one-point shot over five seasons
justification: Two-point GOALS and ATTEMPTS are OBSERVED counts and reconcile exactly (Phase 9 check 8: 1PT + 2PT reconstructs goals and points at team level in all five seasons). Counting them is not the same as estimating who is good at them.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: Two-point production must never be presented as, or silently converted into, two-point ability -- see the row below.

what_it_measures: the share of his team's recorded offensive opportunities (shots + turnovers) a player personally took on
supporting_statistic: the constant model still wins cross-validation on 844 player-seasons with folds cut by player; the usage/offensive-EPA correlation is negative in four of five seasons
justification: Usage is a countable share with a countable numerator and denominator. What it does NOT support is an expectation: five seasons say there is no reliable relationship between how much a player is used and how much value he produces, so a usage-adjusted expectation adds a parameter and no information.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: It is NOT the share of team possessions a player was on the field for. The feed carries no lineup, shift or minutes data of any kind, in any season.

what_it_measures: correcting a player's or team's value for the strength of the opposition faced
supporting_statistic: schedule connectivity 1.00 in every season, but strength-of-schedule spread is only 14-29% of between-team spread and the adjustment moves ranks by 2 places at most
justification: Phase 9 established that this is feasible (all 28 pairings occur every season) and nearly worthless (a balanced round-robin leaves almost nothing to adjust for; in 2026 the adjustment is smaller than its own bootstrap standard error). It is EXPERIMENTAL rather than UNSUPPORTED because it is computable and correct -- just not worth the parameter.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: There is no player-level opponent adjustment anywhere: the feed carries no matchup or assignment data, so 'who did this attackman score against' is not answerable at the defender level.

what_it_measures: caused turnovers above the position group's per-GAME average -- and nothing else about defence
supporting_statistic: in all five seasons, 8434 turnover events carry 0 causing-defender ids and 0 closest-defender ids; caused turnovers correlate with games played at rho 0.64
justification: The three raw fields that would carry individual defensive attribution -- causedTurnoverId, closestDefenderId, commitedTurnoverId -- exist in the schema and are empty in every one of the 51,000+ events of all five seasons. Caused turnovers survive only as a box-score total with no time, no context and no opponent. There is also no minutes, shift or lineup data anywhere, so a defender has no exposure denominator at all.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: PARTIAL must stay in the name. A value of 0.0 means 'caused turnovers at his group's per-game rate, everything else unmeasured', NOT 'an average defender'.

what_it_measures: faceoff wins above the league win probability, priced at the empirical value of a possession-gaining event
supporting_statistic: career kappa 10.4 draws -- five to seven times smaller than any other rate's -- with 54.4% of takers clearing reliability 0.5 and an implied true between-player sd of 0.148
justification: Faceoff is the ONE cleanly identified individual skill in this feed, and as a within-role measure it is READY. It is classified NOT_COMPARABLE because of what happens when it is put next to other roles: it is NULL for roughly four players in five, and the faceoff role supplies 25-75% of the top 20 under most transformations tested in section F while being 5% of the league.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: Undefined for every player who never takes a draw. A model that treats a NULL faceoff value as zero is asserting that not taking draws is exactly average at taking them.

what_it_measures: points allowed on shots on goal faced against league expected points per shot on goal
supporting_statistic: career kappa 495 shots on goal against a median career of 354; 8 of 27 goalies clear reliability 0.5 (one of sixteen in 2026 alone). Pooled EPA_points_raw sd is 7.98 for goalies against 1.74 for close defenders -- 4.6x
justification: Career pooling is the single largest improvement Phase 9/10 found for any rate -- one goalie clears the gate on a season, eight do on a career -- so goalie ABILITY is estimable for about three goalies in ten. Goalie VALUE on the shared EPA scale is not comparable to a field player's: it is measured over 150-400 shots faced where a close defender's entire record is a handful of caused turnovers.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: A goalie's total value is driven substantially by how many shots his team conceded, which is not his action. Counterfactual P4 in cross_position_counterfactuals.csv shows the size of that confound.

what_it_measures: putting roles on one scale so their values can be set side by side
source_metric: EPA_position_z, EPA_position_percentile, and the ten candidates tested in section F
supporting_statistic: role EPA standard deviations differ by 4.6x pooled (3.2-6.4x by season) and role opportunity means by 21x. Only within-position z and percentile equalise the scale, and counterfactual P1 shows why that is not enough: five players who are each +2 SD within their own role receive 2.91 to 18.61 PLL points above their role baseline -- a 6.4x spread -- while receiving identical z-scores of 2.0
justification: Standardisation removes the group effect. It does not establish that a 95th-percentile faceoff specialist and a 95th-percentile attackman contributed equally, and the counterfactual shows they did not contribute equally in points. Quantile-mapping the roles onto a common distribution equalises the scale only by ASSUMING the difference is entirely measurement -- which is the conclusion such a model would need to establish.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: Baseline scope is settled: {'position': 53, 'position_season': 5} of the tested role/component combinations recommend a POSITION baseline rather than a POSITION-SEASON one, because between-season movement is within sampling error.

what_it_measures: an individual player's underlying two-point conversion rate
source_metric: two_point_rate_shrunk (collapsed to the league mean by construction)
supporting_statistic: career: 271 shooters, 2465 attempts, median 3; observed between-player variance 0.010224 is BELOW binomial noise 0.013711 (excess -0.003487); prior capped at 1e6; max reliability 0.000110
justification: Replicated in every season, in the pooled player-seasons, and now on the final career aggregation: the spread between players is no wider than chance alone predicts. Every shrunk value is the league mean and no player is separable from it. The binding constraint is attempts -- a median of 3 across an entire career.
caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: INDIVIDUAL_TWO_POINT_ABILITY = UNSUPPORTED / DO_NOT_USE. This is a statement about identification, not about the shot: two-point PRODUCTION remains a legitimate descriptive statistic.
